parallel.requirements: Recognized the full 84-requirement Jenkins task from the prompt and launched a swarm covering all listed slugs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Assigned implementation ownership to child agents, first one slug per child and later grouped remaining related slugs for a retry.
parallel.implementation: Produced only a partial implementation set: 11 non-empty requirement patch files were present in the final collected workspace.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Patch artifacts were collected by the harness, but no final response or coverage summary was delivered and most requirement patches were absent.
parallel.verification: Some local checks occurred in child work, and official LoopsBench testing later failed the task with only one listed unit passing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Most child agents were aborted before finalizing work; the final state covered 11 of 84 required patch artifacts and failed official evaluation.

serial.requirements: Received the same 84-requirement prompt and read batches of requirement YAML files during a single-agent survey.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used no delegation; Agent and AgentSwarm were disabled, leaving all implementation and verification work on one serial actor.
serial.implementation: Did not produce requirement patch artifacts; the patch timeline remained empty through the final collection point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No implemented requirement patches or final coverage summary were delivered before timeout.
serial.verification: Official LoopsBench testing ran on an effectively unimplemented workspace and reported all listed unit cases failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run was still in survey/planning and requirement reading when it was cancelled/timed out, leaving the whole 84-requirement task unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt required all 84 requirement files, and the parallel parent used that complete slug list for the initial swarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and requirement list, with no evidence of a narrower official task.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the broad 84-item scope; the difference was execution coverage, not task definition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent delegated all requirements to children, then grouped remaining work into 49 child items for a second swarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled Agent and AgentSwarm and kept work in the main session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel established child ownership for many requirements; serial had no child ownership boundary and made slower single-agent progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first child brief gave each child the slug, requirement file path, implementation steps, verification expectations, and required patch workflow; the retry added stricter git isolation instructions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor directly read requirement batches and retained context locally rather than transferring it across child boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The evidence does not show a missing brief or interface contract; the harmful boundary was that child work was interrupted before results arrived.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run produced a small set of requirement diffs, including entries from autocomplete-suggestion-count through user-reload-beta-api.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run's patch timeline remained empty from start through the final snapshot.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented a partial subset; serial did not reach committed requirement implementations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel harness recorded timeout closure after high tool and token usage and two interrupted swarms.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial harness also timed out, with lower token use and no patch artifacts before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit timeout, but parallel spent the budget attempting large child batches while serial spent it in single-agent exploration.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations make this a both_fail pair, not a discordant outcome. The parallel attempt differed materially by creating partial requirement patches, but the interrupted child batches left most requirement work unavailable. The serial control failed for a different process reason: it never delegated and did not reach any committed requirement patch before timeout.
parallel_contributors: Broad AgentSwarm delegation followed by explicit abortion of active child batches.
Only 11 of 84 required patch artifacts existed when the harness collected final outputs.
serial_contributors: Agent and AgentSwarm were disabled, so all work remained in one main session.
The patch timeline remained empty through final collection.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel made partial code/documentation changes for a subset of requirements; serial remained in survey and produced no implementation artifacts.
Both final response files were empty, so neither run delivered the required final coverage count.
evaluator_effects: The official status does not expose passed/total aggregate counts to the resolver; detailed results show one parallel listed unit pass and no serial listed unit passes, but both solution_passed fields are false.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both runs failed; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process event rather than an explanation for a discordant official outcome
